guide.summary: 了 is not a past tense. After a verb it marks one action as done and bounded (often with a counted object); at the end of a sentence it says the situation is new or has changed. Ask two questions: is this a single finished event, and is something different now? If the sentence only describes a habit, a state, or something that did not happen, there is no 了.

subs.label: 了 right after the verb: one finished action
subs.focus: Learner decides that one finished event takes 了 and that with a counted, timed or specific object 了 sits right after the verb, before the number. Classic errors: omitting 了 because 昨天 is there; pushing 了 past a counted object (我买三本书了). Distractors: 过, 着, 的, ∅.

subs.label: 了 at the end: a new situation
subs.focus: Learner sees that the sentence reports a change (not so before, so now) and ends it with 了: after adjectives, ages, times, 会/能, and with 快/要 for 'about to'. Classic error: dropping 了, leaving a plain description. Context or cue must make the change explicit so ∅ is wrong.

subs.label: Verb 了 + amount + 了: so far, and still going
subs.focus: Learner chooses one 了 (amount of a finished action) or two (amount so far, still going). Classic error: one 了 for 'have been doing for ...', or no final 了 after 已经. Force the reading: 已经/到现在/'still' for double; a closed past frame (去年, 以前) for single.

subs.label: Verb 了 + object + 就/再: after doing A, do B
subs.focus: Learner puts 了 after the first verb, before its object, for 'once A is done, B', also in future plans. Classic errors: omitting it, placing it after the object (吃饭了就走), or refusing 了 because it is about tomorrow. Past sequences: a second 了 closes the sentence.

subs.label: No 了 for habits and repeated actions
subs.focus: Learner leaves 了 out for routines and repeated actions, present or past: 每天, 常常, 经常, 总是, 一般, 以前/小时候 + habit. Classic error: adding 了 to a past habit because English has past tense. Answer is ∅. Avoid newly begun habits (现在每天跑步了), where final 了 is right.

subs.label: 没 + verb: no 了
subs.focus: Learner negates a completed action with 没(有) + verb and deletes 了; never 不 + verb + 了 for 'did not'. Classic errors: 我没去了, 我没买了三本书. Rewrites: make a 了 sentence negative. Avoid the legitimate 没…了 patterns (没钱了, 三天没睡觉了, 好久没见了).

subs.label: No 了 for past states: 是, 在, 有, 喜欢, 觉得, adjectives
subs.focus: Learner leaves 了 out when a past sentence describes how things were: 是, 在, 有, 喜欢, 想, 知道, 觉得, 很 + adjective. Classic errors: 昨天很冷了, 他以前是了老师, 我觉得了很好. Pure description only; avoid changed states (天冷了, 我知道了), which take final 了.

subs.label: 太 + adjective + 了
subs.focus: Learner closes a 太 remark with 了 (太贵了, 太好了) and adds no 了 after 很, 非常 or 不太. Classic errors: 太好!, 很贵了 for 'too expensive', 不太冷了 for 'not very cold'. Test as a complete remark ending in the adjective; avoid 太 + adjective inside a longer phrase (太贵的东西).

subs.label: 不 … 了 / 没有 … 了: no longer, not any more
subs.focus: Learner says 'not any more' or a changed plan with 不 + verb + 了 ('none left': 没有 + noun + 了), 了 at the end. Classic errors: dropping 了 (plain 'don't'), 没 + verb for a decision not to go, 了 after the verb. Cues ('any more', 'after all', 已经, 现在) must force the change.

rules.rule: One finished action with a counted, timed or specific object: put 了 directly after the verb, before the number.
rules.pattern: Subject + (time) + Verb + 了 + number + measure + Object

examples.py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le sān běn shū
examples.en: I bought three books yesterday.

examples.py: tā hē le liǎng bēi kā fēi
examples.en: She drank two cups of coffee.

examples.zh: 我们在那儿等了半个小时。
examples.py: wǒ men zài nà r děng le bàn ge xiǎo shí
examples.en: We waited there for half an hour.

examples.py: tā gěi wǒ dǎ le yī ge diàn huà
examples.en: He gave me a call.

rules.note: A time word such as 昨天 does not replace 了: a single finished event still needs it.

rules.rule: With a plain, uncounted object, a simple 'this happened' statement usually puts 了 at the end of the sentence; verb + 了 + bare object alone sounds unfinished.

examples.py: wǒ chī fàn le
examples.en: I've eaten.

examples.py: tā zuó tiān qù shàng hǎi le
examples.en: He went to Shanghai yesterday.

examples.py: wǒ mǎi le nà běn cí diǎn
examples.en: I bought that dictionary.

rules.note: This is a tendency, not a law: a specific object (那本词典) is fine after 了, and 我吃了饭 is fine when more follows (see the sequence pattern). Drill items should use counted or clearly specific objects when testing the position after the verb.

rules.rule: If the sentence means 'it is now so, and it was not before', end it with 了. This works after adjectives, ages, times and 会/能/可以.
rules.pattern: Subject + adjective / Verb phrase / number phrase + 了

examples.py: xià yǔ le
examples.en: It's raining now. (It has started to rain.)

examples.py: wǒ è le wǒ men qù chī fàn ba
examples.en: I'm hungry now, let's go and eat.

examples.py: tā huì kāi chē le
examples.en: He can drive now.

examples.py: wǒ nǚ ér bā suì le
examples.en: My daughter is eight now.

rules.note: Without 了 these are plain descriptions (他会开车 = he can drive); 了 adds 'this is new'.

rules.rule: Something about to happen is a change on its way: 快 / 要 / 快要 / 就要 … 了.
rules.pattern: Subject + 快(要) / 就要 + Verb phrase + 了

examples.py: huǒ chē kuài yào kāi le
examples.en: The train is about to leave.

examples.py: wǒ men kuài dào le
examples.en: We're almost there.

examples.zh: 他们下个月就要结婚了。
examples.py: tā men xià ge yuè jiù yào jié hūn le
examples.en: They are getting married next month.

rules.rule: For 'have done this much so far' (and it is still going on or still counts now), use 了 after the verb and again at the end. One 了 only gives the amount of an action that is over.
rules.pattern: Subject + (已经) + Verb + 了 + duration / amount + (Object) + 了

examples.py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le
examples.en: I've been studying Chinese for two years (and still am).

examples.zh: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
examples.py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
examples.en: He has already had three cups of coffee (so far).

examples.zh: 我们等了半个小时了，他还没来。
examples.py: wǒ men děng le bàn ge xiǎo shí le tā hái méi lái
examples.en: We've been waiting for half an hour and he still hasn't come.

examples.zh: 我以前在上海住了三年。
examples.py: wǒ yǐ qián zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián
examples.en: I lived in Shanghai for three years (in the past).

rules.note: The single-了 sentence is normally understood as finished, but only context (以前, 去年, what comes next) makes that certain. With 已经, the final 了 is expected.

rules.rule: For 'after A, then B', put 了 after the first verb, before its object. This 了 means 'once A is done', so it is used for future plans too.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb1 + 了 + Object1 + 就 / 再 + Verb2

examples.py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù zǒu
examples.en: I'll leave as soon as I've eaten.

examples.py: nǐ xià le kè gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà
examples.en: Call me after class.

examples.py: xǐ le shǒu zài chī fàn
examples.en: Wash your hands before you eat.

examples.zh: 他昨天下了班就回家了。
examples.py: tā zuó tiān xià le bān jiù huí jiā le
examples.en: Yesterday he went home right after work.

rules.note: When the whole sequence is in the past, a second 了 normally closes the sentence, as in the last example. 就 = straight after; 再 = only then.

rules.rule: Habits and repeated actions take no 了, even when they are in the past. Words like 每天, 常常, 经常, 总是 and 一般 are the signal.
rules.pattern: Subject + (以前 / 小时候) + 每天 / 常常 + Verb + Object

examples.py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang hē kā fēi
examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.

examples.py: tā yǐ qián cháng cháng chí dào
examples.en: He often used to be late.

examples.zh: 小时候我每个星期天都去奶奶家。
examples.py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ měi ge xīng qī tiān dōu qù nǎi nai jiā
examples.en: When I was little I went to my grandmother's every Sunday.

rules.note: A final 了 is possible when the habit itself is new (我现在每天跑步了 = I now run every day). That is the change-of-state 了, not this pattern.

rules.rule: To say an action did not happen, use 没(有) + verb and drop 了. Never 不 + verb + 了 for 'did not'.

examples.py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù
examples.en: I didn't go yesterday.

examples.py: tā hái méi chī fàn
examples.en: He hasn't eaten yet.

examples.py: wǒ méi mǎi nà běn shū
examples.en: I didn't buy that book.

rules.note: 没 and 了 do meet in two other patterns that are not negated completed actions: 没有 + noun + 了 (我没有钱了, I'm out of money) and time + 没 + verb + 了 (我三天没睡觉了, I haven't slept for three days).

rules.rule: A past state is not an event. 是, 在, 有, 喜欢, 想, 知道, 觉得 and adjectives take no 了 when you only describe how things were; the time word shows the past.
rules.pattern: Time + Subject + 是 / 在 / 喜欢 / 觉得 / 很 + adjective (no 了)

examples.py: zuó tiān hěn lěng
examples.en: It was cold yesterday.

examples.py: tā qù nián shì wǒ de lǎo shī
examples.en: He was my teacher last year.

examples.py: wǒ xiǎo shí hou hěn xǐ huan yóu yǒng
examples.en: I really liked swimming when I was little.

examples.zh: 我觉得那个电影很有意思。
examples.py: wǒ jué de nà ge diàn yǐng hěn yǒu yì si
examples.en: I thought that film was interesting.

rules.note: The same words can take a final 了 when the state is new: 天冷了 (it has turned cold), 我知道了 (now I know, got it). What is never right is 了 directly after 是, 在 or 觉得 to mean 'was' or 'thought'.

rules.rule: 太 + adjective as a remark ('so ...!', 'too ...') ends in 了. 很, 非常 and 不太 do not take it.

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu tài guì le
examples.en: This piece of clothing is too expensive.

examples.py: tài hǎo le
examples.en: That's great!

examples.py: nǐ tài kè qi le
examples.en: You're too kind.

examples.py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng
examples.en: It's not very cold today.

rules.note: In speech 了 is sometimes dropped, and it is not used when 太 + adjective is only part of a larger phrase (太贵的东西我不买). As a complete remark, include it.

rules.rule: 'Not any more' or 'not after all' is 不 + verb/adjective + 了, with 了 at the end. 'Have none left' is 没有 + noun + 了.
rules.pattern: Subject + 不 + (想 / 能 / 会) + Verb + (Object) + 了

examples.py: wǒ bù hē jiǔ le
examples.en: I don't drink any more.

examples.py: tā bù zài zhè r gōng zuò le
examples.en: He doesn't work here any more.

examples.py: tài wǎn le wǒ bù qù le
examples.en: It's too late, I'm not going after all.

examples.py: wǒ méi yǒu qián le
examples.en: I have no money left.

rules.note: Compare 我没去 (I didn't go: a fact about the past) with 我不去了 (I've changed my mind and am not going).

right.py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le sān běn shū

contrasts.why: 昨天 gives the time but does not mark the action as done. One finished event with a counted object needs 了 right after the verb.
没 already says the action did not happen, so there is nothing for 了 to mark as completed.

right.py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang hē kā fēi

contrasts.why: 每天 makes this a routine, not one finished event. Habits take no 了.
English 'was' tempts you to add 了, but this describes a state. 昨天 already shows it is past.

right.py: tā yǐ qián shì wǒ de lǎo shī
right.en: He used to be my teacher.

contrasts.why: 是 is not an action that can be completed; 是了 never means 'was'. 以前 carries the past.

right.py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù zhǎo nǐ
right.en: I'll come and find you as soon as I've eaten.

contrasts.why: In 'after A, then B', 了 goes straight after the first verb, before its object, even though this is about the future.

right.py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le
right.en: I've been studying Chinese for two years (and still am).

contrasts.why: The one-了 sentence is grammatical but says the wrong thing: the two years sound like a closed chapter. For 'so far, and still going' add the second 了 at the end.
An exclamation with 太 is closed by 了; without it the remark sounds cut off.

right.py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù zhù zài běi jīng le
right.en: I don't live in Beijing any more.

contrasts.why: 'No longer' is a change of situation, so 不 … needs 了 at the end. Without 了 it is only a plain 'don't', which does not fit 已经.

right.py: xià yǔ le wǒ men bié chū qù le
right.en: It's raining, let's not go out.

contrasts.why: The rain is a new situation, so the clause needs 了 at the end. Bare 下雨 does not report that it has started.

cheat: One finished event with a number or duration? 了 goes right after the verb, before the number.
Something is different now (now hungry, now eight, now able, about to)? 了 at the very end.
'So far, and still going' or 已经 + amount? Two 了: after the verb and at the end.
'After A, then B' with 就 or 再? Verb + 了 + object in the first half, past or future.
每天, 常常, 总是, or a past state with 是 / 在 / 喜欢 / 觉得 / 很 + adjective? No 了.
没 + verb means it did not happen: delete 了.
太 … 了 for 'so / too'; 不 … 了 for 'not any more'.

items.q: 老师昨天给我们留___三篇作业。
items.zh: 老师昨天给我们留了三篇作业。
items.py: lǎo shī zuó tiān gěi wǒ men liú le sān piān zuò yè
items.en: The teacher assigned us three pieces of homework yesterday.
items.why: One finished event with a counted object: 了 goes right after 留, before 三篇. 昨天 gives the time but cannot replace 了, so leaving it out fails; 着 describes a continuing state, not a finished act.

items.q: 我今天上午喝___两杯茶。
items.zh: 我今天上午喝了两杯茶。
items.py: wǒ jīn tiān shàng wǔ hē le liǎng bēi chá
items.en: I drank two cups of tea this morning.
items.why: The drinking is finished and the object is counted (两杯), so 了 sits right after 喝. Without it the sentence reads like a plan or a general statement, and 着 or 的 cannot mark a completed act.

items.q: 经理上午给我们开___一个会。
items.zh: 经理上午给我们开了一个会。
items.py: jīng lǐ shàng wǔ gěi wǒ men kāi le yí gè huì
items.en: The manager held a meeting for us this morning.
items.why: A single completed meeting with a counted noun takes 了 right after 开. 着 would make the meeting ongoing, and 的 turns 开 into a modifier of 一个会 instead of reporting the event.

items.q: 我们在图书馆复习___三个小时就回家了。
items.zh: 我们在图书馆复习了三个小时就回家了。
items.py: wǒ men zài tú shū guǎn fù xí le sān gè xiǎo shí jiù huí jiā le
items.en: We revised in the library for three hours and then went home.
items.why: A bounded stretch of time that ended (and was followed by going home) takes 了 after the verb. 过 is about having done something at some point in life, which does not fit a specific afternoon.

items.q: 小李上个星期写___五份报告。
items.zh: 小李上个星期写了五份报告。
items.py: xiǎo lǐ shàng gè xīng qī xiě le wǔ fèn bào gào
items.en: Last week Xiao Li wrote five reports.
items.why: 上个星期 is a closed past time and 五份报告 is a counted object, so 了 follows 写. A time word alone does not mark completion; 着 and 的 do not report a finished action.

items.q: 这次考试他考___八十分，老师很满意。
items.zh: 这次考试他考了八十分，老师很满意。
items.py: zhè cì kǎo shì tā kǎo le bā shí fēn lǎo shī hěn mǎn yì
items.en: He scored eighty on this exam and the teacher was pleased.
items.why: A result reached once, with a number, takes 了 right after the verb 考. 的 would need a noun to follow (考的成绩), and 着 gives an ongoing state; neither reports what happened.

items.q: 我上周三发___两封邮件给客户。
items.zh: 我上周三发了两封邮件给客户。
items.py: wǒ shàng zhōu sān fā le liǎng fēng yóu jiàn gěi kè hù
items.en: Last Wednesday I sent two emails to the client.
items.why: A completed action on a specific past day with a counted object needs 了 after 发. Without it, 两封邮件 reads like an instruction or plan, and 着 does not fit a one-off sending.

items.q: 为了准备明天的考试，我昨天晚上复习___整整四个小时的语法。
items.zh: 为了准备明天的考试，我昨天晚上复习了整整四个小时的语法。
items.py: wèi le zhǔn bèi míng tiān de kǎo shì wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shàng fù xí le zhěng zhěng sì gè xiǎo shí de yǔ fǎ
items.en: To prepare for tomorrow's exam, I spent a full four hours revising grammar last night.
items.why: The revising is over and bounded by 四个小时, so 了 goes right after 复习 even though the sentence mentions tomorrow. Leaving it out loses the sense of a finished event; 着 cannot take a time span.

items.q: 财务部上个月招___两个新同事，一个负责报销，一个负责工资。
items.zh: 财务部上个月招了两个新同事，一个负责报销，一个负责工资。
items.py: cái wù bù shàng gè yuè zhāo le liǎng gè xīn tóng shì yí gè fù zé bào xiāo yí gè fù zé gōng zī
items.en: Last month the finance department hired two new colleagues, one for expenses and one for payroll.
items.why: Hiring happened once last month and the object is counted, so 了 follows 招. 着 would mean the hiring is in progress, and 的 would make 招的两个新同事 a noun phrase with nothing to finish the sentence.

items.zh: 同学昨天借了两本词典。
items.py: tóng xué zuó tiān jiè le liǎng běn cí diǎn
items.en: My classmate borrowed two dictionaries yesterday.
items.why: With a counted object, 了 sits right after the verb 借 and before 两本词典. Leaving it for the end of the sentence is the tempting wrong order.

items.zh: 小李给客户发了两封邮件。
items.py: xiǎo lǐ gěi kè hù fā le liǎng fēng yóu jiàn
items.en: Xiao Li sent the client two emails.
items.why: The finished action takes 了 directly after 发, before the counted object 两封邮件. The 给客户 phrase stays before the verb.

items.zh: 他今天下午在会议室开了三个小时的会。
items.py: tā jīn tiān xià wǔ zài huì yì shì kāi le sān gè xiǎo shí de huì
items.en: This afternoon he spent three hours in a meeting in the meeting room.
items.why: A finished, timed event puts 了 right after 开, before 三个小时的会. Moving 了 to the end would change the sense to 'has been in a meeting for three hours so far'. The place phrase 在会议室 stays before the verb.

items.task: Say he drank two cups (add 两杯).
items.zh: 他喝了两杯咖啡。
items.py: tā hē le liǎng bēi kā fēi
items.en: He drank two cups of coffee.
items.why: Once the object is counted, 了 moves right after the verb and ends up before 两杯. The final 了 of the source sentence is no longer needed.

items.task: Say it happened: we waited for her for half an hour.
items.zh: 我们等了她半个小时。
items.py: wǒ men děng le tā bàn gè xiǎo shí
items.en: We waited for her for half an hour.
items.why: A finished stretch of waiting with a stated duration takes 了 right after the verb. The pronoun object 她 comes before the duration.

items.s: 老师昨天讲三个语法点。
items.s_py: lǎo shī zuó tiān jiǎng sān gè yǔ fǎ diǎn
items.zh: 老师昨天讲了三个语法点。
items.py: lǎo shī zuó tiān jiǎng le sān gè yǔ fǎ diǎn
items.en: The teacher covered three grammar points yesterday.
items.why: A finished event with a counted object needs 了 right after the verb. 昨天 shows the time but cannot replace 了; without it the sentence sounds like a plan or an unfinished clause.

items.s: 经理昨天去上海了。
items.s_py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān qù shàng hǎi le
items.zh: 经理昨天去上海了。
items.py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān qù shàng hǎi le
items.en: The manager went to Shanghai yesterday.
items.why: This is correct: with a plain place object and no number, a simple report of a finished trip puts 了 at the end of the sentence. It is not wrong to leave 了 off the verb here.

items.s: 小王写了那份报告。
items.s_py: xiǎo wáng xiě le nà fèn bào gào
items.zh: 小王写了那份报告。
items.py: xiǎo wáng xiě le nà fèn bào gào
items.en: Xiao Wang wrote that report.
items.why: This is correct: 那份报告 is a specific object, so 了 may follow the verb directly. Learners often think verb + 了 needs a number, but a specific object works just as well.

items.s: 上个星期公司招两个新同事，他们都是学经济的。
items.s_py: shàng gè xīng qī gōng sī zhāo liǎng gè xīn tóng shì tā men dōu shì xué jīng jì de
items.zh: 上个星期公司招了两个新同事，他们都是学经济的。
items.py: shàng gè xīng qī gōng sī zhāo le liǎng gè xīn tóng shì tā men dōu shì xué jīng jì de
items.en: Last week the company hired two new colleagues, both of whom studied economics.
items.why: The hiring is a single finished event with a counted object, so 招 needs 了. 上个星期 is only a time word; without 了 the clause sounds like a plan, not a fact.

items.q: 天黑___，我们回家吧。
items.zh: 天黑了，我们回家吧。
items.py: tiān hēi le wǒ men huí jiā ba
items.en: It's dark now, let's go home.
items.why: Sentence-final 了 reports a new situation: it was light, now it is dark. 过 and 着 do not mark a change, and 的 would make 天黑的 a noun-like phrase.

items.q: 刚才不饿，现在我饿___。
items.zh: 刚才不饿，现在我饿了。
items.py: gāng cái bù è xiàn zài wǒ è le
items.en: I wasn't hungry a moment ago, but now I am.
items.why: The cue says a change happened (not hungry before, hungry now), so the sentence ends with 了. 饿 with nothing after it describes a state with no hint of change, which contradicts 刚才不饿.

items.q: 我女儿已经八岁___，该上学了。
items.zh: 我女儿已经八岁了，该上学了。
items.py: wǒ nǚ ér yǐ jīng bā suì le gāi shàng xué le
items.en: My daughter is already eight, so it is time for her to start school.
items.why: An age reached now is a new situation, and 已经 asks for 了 at the end: 八岁了. 的 and 着 cannot close an age expression.

items.q: 小王学了三个月，现在会用这个软件___。
items.zh: 小王学了三个月，现在会用这个软件了。
items.py: xiǎo wáng xué le sān gè yuè xiàn zài huì yòng zhè ge ruǎn jiàn le
items.en: Xiao Wang has studied for three months, and now he can use this software.
items.why: 会 + verb + 了 says he has newly acquired the skill. 过 would mean he has used it before, and 着 or 的 does not close the sentence.

items.q: 快考试___，同学们都在复习。
items.zh: 快考试了，同学们都在复习。
items.py: kuài kǎo shì le tóng xué men dōu zài fù xí
items.en: The exam is about to start and everyone is revising.
items.why: 快 … 了 frames an event that is about to happen as a change on its way. 过 and 着 do not fit 快, and 的 is not a closing particle here.

items.q: 现在已经十一点___，你该睡觉了。
items.zh: 现在已经十一点了，你该睡觉了。
items.py: xiàn zài yǐ jīng shí yī diǎn le nǐ gāi shuì jiào le
items.en: It's already eleven o'clock, you should go to bed.
items.why: A clock time reached now, with 已经, is a changed situation and takes final 了. 的 and 着 do not close a time expression, and 过 would shift the meaning to 'has passed eleven in the past'.

items.q: 会议下个月就要开始___，我们得赶紧把材料准备好。
items.zh: 会议下个月就要开始了，我们得赶紧把材料准备好。
items.py: huì yì xià gè yuè jiù yào kāi shǐ le wǒ men dé gǎn jǐn bǎ cái liào zhǔn bèi hǎo
items.en: The conference starts next month, so we have to get the materials ready quickly.
items.why: 就要 … 了 marks something that is about to happen. 着 and 过 cannot follow 开始 in this pattern, and 的 would turn 就要开始 into a modifier without a closing sentence.

items.q: 天气渐渐冷___，办公室里也开始开暖气了。
items.zh: 天气渐渐冷了，办公室里也开始开暖气了。
items.py: tiān qì jiàn jiàn lěng le bàn gōng shì lǐ yě kāi shǐ kāi nuǎn qì le
items.en: The weather has gradually turned cold and the office has started to turn on the heating.
items.why: The 渐渐 shows a change in progress, so the adjective 冷 takes final 了 for 'has become cold'. 着 would mean it stays cold, and 过 would mean it was cold at some earlier point.

items.zh: 考试快要开始了。
items.py: kǎo shì kuài yào kāi shǐ le
items.en: The exam is about to start.
items.why: 快要 … 了 wraps around the verb: it frames the coming event as a change under way. 了 must close the sentence, not follow 快要.

items.zh: 他现在会说汉语了。
items.py: tā xiàn zài huì shuō hàn yǔ le
items.en: He can speak Chinese now.
items.why: 现在 and 了 together say this is a new ability: 了 goes at the end after the whole verb phrase. Without it the sentence is a plain statement about ability.

items.task: Say he can drive now (he has just learned).
items.zh: 他会开车了。
items.py: tā huì kāi chē le
items.en: He can drive now.
items.why: Adding sentence-final 了 turns the plain ability statement into a new situation: he did not use to be able to drive, but now he can.

items.s: 火车快了要开。
items.s_py: huǒ chē kuài le yào kāi
items.zh: 火车快要开了。
items.py: huǒ chē kuài yào kāi le
items.en: The train is about to leave.
items.why: 快要 is a unit and 了 closes the clause after the verb: 快要开了. Splitting 快 and 要 with 了 is not possible.

items.s: 我儿子五岁了。
items.s_py: wǒ ér zi wǔ suì le
items.zh: 我儿子五岁了。
items.py: wǒ ér zi wǔ suì le
items.en: My son is five now.
items.why: This is correct: an age takes sentence-final 了 when it has just been reached. It looks odd to learners because 了 follows a number, not a verb.

items.s: 我们的新同事已经会用这个系统了。
items.s_py: wǒ men de xīn tóng shì yǐ jīng huì yòng zhè ge xì tǒng le
items.zh: 我们的新同事已经会用这个系统了。
items.py: wǒ men de xīn tóng shì yǐ jīng huì yòng zhè ge xì tǒng le
items.en: Our new colleague can already use this system.
items.why: This is correct: 已经 + 会 + verb phrase + 了 says the skill is now in place. The 了 at the end marks the change, not a completed action.

items.q: 我已经学___两年中文___。
items.zh: 我已经学了两年中文了。
items.py: wǒ yǐ jīng xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le
items.en: I've been studying Chinese for two years now.
items.why: Time so far and still going: 了 after the verb for the amount, a second 了 at the end for 'up to now'. With 已经, one 了 alone reads as a closed stretch, and with no 了 it is not marked as done at all.

items.q: 他到现在已经喝___三杯咖啡___。
items.zh: 他到现在已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
items.py: tā dào xiàn zài yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
items.en: So far he has already drunk three cups of coffee.
items.why: 到现在 and 已经 make this a count so far: 了 after 喝 for the amount and 了 at the end for 'up to now'. With one 了 the three cups sound finished and closed; with none, nothing marks the count as done.

items.q: 我们等___一个小时___，经理还没来。
items.zh: 我们等了一个小时了，经理还没来。
items.py: wǒ men děng le yí gè xiǎo shí le jīng lǐ hái méi lái
items.en: We've been waiting for an hour and the manager still hasn't come.
items.why: 还没来 shows the waiting is still going on: 了 after the verb for the amount, 了 at the end for 'so far'. 着 cannot take a time span, and with no 了 the hour is not marked as done at all.

items.q: 我去年在上海住___三个月___。
items.zh: 我去年在上海住了三个月。
items.py: wǒ qù nián zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān gè yuè
items.en: Last year I lived in Shanghai for three months.
items.why: 去年 closes the time frame: the three months are over, so one 了 after the verb is enough. A second final 了 would claim the stay still counts up to now, which clashes with 去年.

items.q: 小李以前在这家公司工作___五年___，后来去了别的公司。
items.zh: 小李以前在这家公司工作了五年，后来去了别的公司。
items.py: xiǎo lǐ yǐ qián zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò le wǔ nián hòu lái qù le bié de gōng sī
items.en: Xiao Li used to work at this company for five years before moving to another one.
items.why: 后来去了别的公司 shows the five years ended in the past, so only the verb 了 is used. The final 了 would say he is still there, which contradicts the sentence.

items.q: 我已经在这个办公室坐___整整八个小时___，腰都疼了。
items.zh: 我已经在这个办公室坐了整整八个小时了，腰都疼了。
items.py: wǒ yǐ jīng zài zhè ge bàn gōng shì zuò le zhěng zhěng bā gè xiǎo shí le yāo dōu téng le
items.en: I've been sitting in this office for a full eight hours already, and my back is sore.
items.why: 已经 and the ongoing sitting give 'so far': 了 after 坐 and 了 at the end after 小时. 着 cannot take a time span, and with no 了 nothing marks the eight hours as counted up to now.

items.zh: 他已经工作了三年了。
items.py: tā yǐ jīng gōng zuò le sān nián le
items.en: He has already been working for three years.
items.why: 已经 asks for two 了: one after 工作 for the length of time and one at the end for 'so far'. A single 了 would turn it into a closed stretch of time.

items.src_py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián yīng yǔ
items.task: Say you have been studying for two years and still are.
items.zh: 我学了两年英语了。
items.py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián yīng yǔ le
items.en: I've been studying English for two years now.
items.why: Adding a second 了 at the end turns the closed amount into 'so far, still going'. The first 了 stays right after the verb.

items.s: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
items.s_py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
items.zh: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
items.py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
items.en: He has already had three cups of coffee.
items.why: This is correct: 已经 plus a counted amount takes both 了, one after the verb and one at the end. It looks like a repeated 了 error but is the standard 'so far' pattern.

items.s: 她小时候在上海住了三年了，后来搬到了北京。
items.s_py: tā xiǎo shí hou zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián le hòu lái bān dào le běi jīng
items.zh: 她小时候在上海住了三年，后来搬到了北京。
items.py: tā xiǎo shí hou zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián hòu lái bān dào le běi jīng
items.en: When she was little she lived in Shanghai for three years, and later moved to Beijing.
items.why: 后来搬到了北京 shows the three years are over, so only one 了 is used. The final 了 would claim she still counts those years up to now, which contradicts moving away.

items.q: 我吃___饭就去上课。
items.zh: 我吃了饭就去上课。
items.py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù shàng kè
items.en: I'll go to class as soon as I've eaten.
items.why: In 'after A, then B', 了 follows the first verb, before its object. It marks that A is done, and 着 (still eating) or 的 does not give that sense.

items.q: 下___课，我们就去吃饭。
items.zh: 下了课，我们就去吃饭。
items.py: xià le kè wǒ men jiù qù chī fàn
items.en: After class we'll go and eat.
items.why: 下了课 means 'once class is over', and 就 links it to the next step. 着 cannot attach to 下 here, and 过 would mean a past experience.

items.q: 你写___作业再玩手机。
items.zh: 你写了作业再玩手机。
items.py: nǐ xiě le zuò yè zài wán shǒu jī
items.en: Finish your homework before you play with your phone.
items.why: 写了作业再玩手机 says do the second thing once the first is finished. 着 would mean doing both at once, and 在 is not a particle that goes after the verb.

items.q: 他昨天下___班就回家了。
items.zh: 他昨天下了班就回家了。
items.py: tā zuó tiān xià le bān jiù huí jiā le
items.en: Yesterday he went home as soon as he finished work.
items.why: In 下了班就 ... the 了 after 下 shows work was over before he left. 着 and 过 do not fit, and 的 would turn 下班 into a modifier.

items.q: 明天开___会，我们再讨论这个问题。
items.zh: 明天开了会，我们再讨论这个问题。
items.py: míng tiān kāi le huì wǒ men zài tǎo lùn zhè ge wèn tí
items.en: After tomorrow's meeting we'll discuss this problem.
items.why: Even in the future, 了 after the first verb says once that step is finished, then 再 brings the next. 着 would mean discussing during the meeting, and 在 does not follow a verb.

items.q: 等我吃___午饭，看___那份文件，就给你回电话。
items.zh: 等我吃了午饭，看了那份文件，就给你回电话。
items.py: děng wǒ chī le wǔ fàn kàn le nà fèn wén jiàn jiù gěi nǐ huí diàn huà
items.en: After I've had lunch and looked at that document, I'll call you back.
items.why: Both steps happen before 就, so each first verb takes 了: 吃了午饭 and 看了那份文件. 着 would mean the steps are happening at once, which cannot lead into 就.

items.zh: 我吃了两个面包就去上课。
items.py: wǒ chī le liǎng gè miàn bāo jiù qù shàng kè
items.en: I'll go to class as soon as I've eaten two rolls.
items.why: 了 sits right after 吃, before the counted object 两个面包, and 就 then links the next step. 了 cannot go after 面包 because it marks the first step as done.

items.zh: 你写了报告再回家。
items.py: nǐ xiě le bào gào zài huí jiā
items.en: Finish the report before you go home.
items.why: Verb 了 + object, then 再 + the next action: 写了报告再回家. 再 means only then, so the order of the two steps cannot be reversed.

items.zh: 他昨天开了一个会就去机场了。
items.py: tā zuó tiān kāi le yí gè huì jiù qù jī chǎng le
items.en: Yesterday he went to the airport right after a meeting.
items.why: In a past sequence, 了 follows 开 (before the counted 一个会) and a second 了 closes the sentence. 昨天 may precede or follow the subject.

items.src: 我吃完这碗面，然后去上班。
items.src_py: wǒ chī wán zhè wǎn miàn rán hòu qù shàng bān
items.task: Combine into one sentence with 就 (once I've eaten, I go).
items.zh: 我吃了这碗面就去上班。
items.py: wǒ chī le zhè wǎn miàn jiù qù shàng bān
items.en: I'll go to work as soon as I've eaten this bowl of noodles.
items.why: 'After A, then B' with 就 uses verb + 了 + object for the first step, and 就 joins the second. The pair 吃完 + 然后 becomes one sentence.

items.s: 你洗手再吃了饭。
items.s_py: nǐ xǐ shǒu zài chī le fàn
items.zh: 你洗了手再吃饭。
items.py: nǐ xǐ le shǒu zài chī fàn
items.en: Wash your hands before you eat.
items.why: 了 belongs after the first step (洗了手), because it marks that step as done before 再. Putting it after 吃 would make eating the completed step instead.

items.s: 明天我们开了会再决定要不要买。
items.s_py: míng tiān wǒ men kāi le huì zài jué dìng yào bù yào mǎi
items.zh: 明天我们开了会再决定要不要买。
items.py: míng tiān wǒ men kāi le huì zài jué dìng yào bù yào mǎi
items.en: Tomorrow we'll hold the meeting first and then decide whether to buy it.
items.why: This is correct: 了 after the first verb in a 再 sequence is used for the future too. It is a trap because 明天 makes learners reject 了.

items.q: 我每天早上六点起___床。
items.zh: 我每天早上六点起床。
items.py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shàng liù diǎn qǐ chuáng
items.en: I get up at six every morning.
items.why: 每天 makes this a routine, and routines take no 了. 了 would mean one finished event of getting up, which clashes with 每天.

items.q: 他常常在图书馆看___书。
items.zh: 他常常在图书馆看书。
items.py: tā cháng cháng zài tú shū guǎn kàn shū
items.en: He often reads in the library.
items.why: 常常 marks a repeated habit, so there is no 了. Adding 了 turns it into one completed reading event, which does not fit 常常.

items.q: 上大学的时候，我每天都在食堂吃___早饭。
items.zh: 上大学的时候，我每天都在食堂吃早饭。
items.py: shàng dà xué de shí hòu wǒ měi tiān dōu zài shí táng chī zǎo fàn
items.en: When I was at university I ate breakfast in the canteen every day.
items.why: The sentence is about the past, but 每天都 makes it a habit. Past habits take no 了 in Chinese, even though English uses the past tense.

items.q: 以前老师总是让我们背___课文。
items.zh: 以前老师总是让我们背课文。
items.py: yǐ qián lǎo shī zǒng shì ràng wǒ men bèi kè wén
items.en: The teacher always used to make us memorise the texts.
items.why: 总是 describes a repeated pattern in the past, so there is no 了. A 了 after 背 would turn it into a single completed act.

items.q: 刚上班的时候，经理一般都会在周一早上开___会，讨论这个星期的安排。
items.zh: 刚上班的时候，经理一般都会在周一早上开会，讨论这个星期的安排。
items.py: gāng shàng bān de shí hòu jīng lǐ yì bān dū huì zài zhōu yī zǎo shàng kāi huì tǎo lùn zhè ge xīng qī de ān pái
items.en: When I first started working, the manager usually held a meeting on Monday mornings to discuss the week's plans.
items.why: 一般都会 marks a regular routine, so 开会 stays bare. 了 would claim one completed meeting, which clashes with 一般 and with the habit of weekly meetings.

items.src_py: wǒ zuó tiān qù tú shū guǎn le
items.task: Say you go to the library every day (a habit).
items.zh: 我每天去图书馆。
items.py: wǒ měi tiān qù tú shū guǎn
items.en: I go to the library every day.
items.why: 每天 turns the sentence into a routine, and routines carry no 了. The 了 of the single-event source must be dropped.

items.s: 他以前每天骑了自行车去学校。
items.s_py: tā yǐ qián měi tiān qí le zì xíng chē qù xué xiào
items.zh: 他以前每天骑自行车去学校。
items.py: tā yǐ qián měi tiān qí zì xíng chē qù xué xiào
items.en: He used to cycle to school every day.
items.why: 每天 marks a habit, so 骑 takes no 了 even though it is in the past. 了 would suggest one finished ride, which clashes with 每天.

items.s: 以前我们每个星期都要考试，所以大家都很紧张。
items.s_py: yǐ qián wǒ men měi gè xīng qī dōu yào kǎo shì suǒ yǐ dà jiā dōu hěn jǐn zhāng
items.zh: 以前我们每个星期都要考试，所以大家都很紧张。
items.py: yǐ qián wǒ men měi gè xīng qī dōu yào kǎo shì suǒ yǐ dà jiā dōu hěn jǐn zhāng
items.en: In the old days we had a test every week, so everyone was tense.
items.why: This is correct: a past habit and a past state both take no 了, and 以前 carries the past. Learners often want a 了 after 考试 because of English past tense.

items.q: 同学们都没做___作业。
items.zh: 同学们都没做作业。
items.py: tóng xué men dōu méi zuò zuò yè
items.en: None of the students did the homework.
items.why: 没 already says the action did not happen, so 了 cannot be added. 没做了作业 would mix a negation with a completed-action marker.

items.q: 他还没吃___午饭。
items.zh: 他还没吃午饭。
items.py: tā hái méi chī wǔ fàn
items.en: He hasn't eaten lunch yet.
items.why: 还没 + verb says it has not happened yet, so 了 is never added. 了 marks that something is completed and contradicts 还没.

items.q: 我昨天___去上课。
items.zh: 我昨天没去上课。
items.py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù shàng kè
items.en: I didn't go to class yesterday.
items.why: To say an action did not happen, use 没 + verb. 不 + verb is for habits or refusals, not for 'did not' in the past, and 别 is a command.

items.q: 作业太难了，我们小组到现在还___做完。
items.zh: 作业太难了，我们小组到现在还没做完。
items.py: zuò yè tài nán le wǒ men xiǎo zǔ dào xiàn zài hái méi zuò wán
items.en: The homework is too hard; our group still hasn't finished it.
items.why: 还 + 没 + verb says an action has not been completed yet. 不做完 would mean a refusal to finish, and 别 is a command.

items.q: 虽然老师提醒了好几次，可是他还是没有按时交___作业。
items.zh: 虽然老师提醒了好几次，可是他还是没有按时交作业。
items.py: suī rán lǎo shī tí xǐng le hǎo jǐ cì kě shì tā hái shì méi yǒu àn shí jiāo zuò yè
items.en: Although the teacher reminded him several times, he still didn't hand in his homework on time.
items.why: 没有 already negates the event, so 交作业 takes no 了. Learners are tempted to add 了 because the sentence is about the past and the earlier clause has 了.

items.zh: 他昨天没有来上班。
items.py: tā zuó tiān méi yǒu lái shàng bān
items.en: He didn't come to work yesterday.
items.why: 没有 sits directly before the verb and nothing else is needed: no 了. The time word 昨天 can come before or after the subject.

items.zh: 我没去学校。
items.py: wǒ méi qù xué xiào
items.en: I didn't go to school.
items.why: Negating a completed action replaces verb + 了 with 没 + verb. 了 must be deleted, and 不 is not used for 'did not'.

items.src: 他昨天给经理发了邮件。
items.src_py: tā zuó tiān gěi jīng lǐ fà le yóu jiàn
items.zh: 他昨天没给经理发邮件。
items.py: tā zuó tiān méi gěi jīng lǐ fà yóu jiàn
items.en: He didn't send the manager an email yesterday.
items.why: The negative of a finished action is 没 + verb with no 了. 没 goes before the whole verb phrase that follows the subject and time word.

items.s: 我昨天没买了三本书。
items.s_py: wǒ zuó tiān méi mǎi le sān běn shū
items.zh: 我昨天没买三本书。
items.py: wǒ zuó tiān méi mǎi sān běn shū
items.en: I didn't buy three books yesterday.
items.why: 没 and verb + 了 cannot appear together: 没 already says it did not happen. 没买了 is a classic error and a native speaker hears it as plainly wrong.

items.s: 他还没来上班，可能路上堵车了。
items.s_py: tā hái méi lái shàng bān kě néng lù shàng dǔ chē le
items.zh: 他还没来上班，可能路上堵车了。
items.py: tā hái méi lái shàng bān kě néng lù shàng dǔ chē le
items.en: He hasn't come to work yet; maybe he's stuck in traffic.
items.why: This is correct: 还没来上班 has no 了, while the second clause 堵车了 is a separate new situation with its own final 了. They do not clash.

items.q: 昨天天气很冷___，我们没去操场。
items.zh: 昨天天气很冷，我们没去操场。
items.py: zuó tiān tiān qì hěn lěng wǒ men méi qù cāo chǎng
items.en: It was cold yesterday, so we didn't go to the sports field.
items.why: This describes how things were, not an event, and 昨天 shows it is past. 了 would suggest it just turned cold, and 很 + adjective takes none.

items.q: 他以前是___我的同学。
items.zh: 他以前是我的同学。
items.py: tā yǐ qián shì wǒ de tóng xué
items.en: He used to be my classmate.
items.why: 是 is not an action that can be completed, so 是了 never means 'was'. 以前 carries the past, and the sentence needs nothing more.

items.q: 我觉得___这次考试很难。
items.zh: 我觉得这次考试很难。
items.py: wǒ jué de zhè cì kǎo shì hěn nán
items.en: I thought this exam was difficult.
items.why: 觉得 is a mental state, not a finished action, so it takes no 了 even when the opinion is about the past. 了 would suggest the thought just changed.

items.q: 小时候我很喜欢___语文课，不太喜欢数学课。
items.zh: 小时候我很喜欢语文课，不太喜欢数学课。
items.py: xiǎo shí hòu wǒ hěn xǐ huān yǔ wén kè bù tài xǐ huān shù xué kè
items.en: As a child I really liked Chinese class but didn't care much for maths.
items.why: 喜欢 is a state of liking, so no 了 even for something in the past. The time phrase 小时候 already places it in the past.

items.q: 当时我不知道___他是新来的经理，所以没有跟他打招呼。
items.zh: 当时我不知道他是新来的经理，所以没有跟他打招呼。
items.py: dāng shí wǒ bù zhī dào tā shì xīn lái de jīng lǐ suǒ yǐ méi yǒu gēn tā dǎ zhāo hū
items.en: At the time I didn't know he was the new manager, so I didn't greet him.
items.why: 知道 here is a past state of not knowing, and 不 + 知道 takes no 了. 当时 sets the time. The change-of-state 我知道了 is a different use.

items.zh: 昨天办公室里很热。
items.py: zuó tiān bàn gōng shì lǐ hěn rè
items.en: It was hot in the office yesterday.
items.why: A past state with 很 + adjective takes no 了: 昨天 supplies the past. The tiles must not include 了.

items.s: 他去年是了我们的数学老师。
items.s_py: tā qù nián shì le wǒ men de shù xué lǎo shī
items.zh: 他去年是我们的数学老师。
items.py: tā qù nián shì wǒ men de shù xué lǎo shī
items.en: Last year he was our maths teacher.
items.why: 是 never takes 了 to mean 'was'; it describes a state, and 去年 already says it was in the past. 是了 is a plain error.

items.s: 昨天晚上办公室里一个人都没有，只有我在加班。
items.s_py: zuó tiān wǎn shàng bàn gōng shì lǐ yí gè rén dōu méi yǒu zhǐ yǒu wǒ zài jiā bān
items.zh: 昨天晚上办公室里一个人都没有，只有我在加班。
items.py: zuó tiān wǎn shàng bàn gōng shì lǐ yí gè rén dōu méi yǒu zhǐ yǒu wǒ zài jiā bān
items.en: Last night there was nobody in the office; only I was working overtime.
items.why: This is correct: 没有 describes a past state, and 在加班 is an action in progress. Neither needs 了, even though learners want one for 'was nobody'.

items.q: 这本书太贵___，我不买。
items.zh: 这本书太贵了，我不买。
items.py: zhè běn shū tài guì le wǒ bù mǎi
items.en: This book is too expensive, I'm not buying it.
items.why: 太 + adjective as a remark is closed by 了: 太贵了. 的 and 着 cannot close it, and 吧 would turn it into a suggestion.

items.q: 你的汉语太好___！
items.zh: 你的汉语太好了！
items.py: nǐ de hàn yǔ tài hǎo le
items.en: Your Chinese is so good!
items.why: The exclamatory 太好了 is closed by 了. 的 would need a noun after it, and 吗 or 吧 would turn the compliment into a question or a guess.

items.q: 这次考试太难___，很多同学都没及格。
items.zh: 这次考试太难了，很多同学都没及格。
items.py: zhè cì kǎo shì tài nán le hěn duō tóng xué dōu méi jí gé
items.en: This exam was too hard, and many students failed.
items.why: 太 + adjective needs 了 to close the remark: 太难了. 着 does not close an adjective, and 的 would mean the adjective is modifying a noun.

items.q: 这个星期作业太多___，我周末也得写。
items.zh: 这个星期作业太多了，我周末也得写。
items.py: zhè ge xīng qī zuò yè tài duō le wǒ zhōu mò yě dé xiě
items.en: There is too much homework this week, so I have to write it over the weekend too.
items.why: The complaint 太多了 ends in 了. 的 would need a noun (太多的作业), and 着 or 过 cannot close an adjective.

items.q: 老板要我们今天就交方案，时间太紧___，恐怕来不及。
items.zh: 老板要我们今天就交方案，时间太紧了，恐怕来不及。
items.py: lǎo bǎn yào wǒ men jīn tiān jiù jiāo fāng àn shí jiān tài jǐn le kǒng pà lái bù jí
items.en: The boss wants the proposal today, and time is too tight, so I'm afraid we won't make it.
items.why: A comment of the 太 + adjective type is closed by 了: 太紧了. 着 and 过 do not close an adjective, and 的 would require a noun to follow.

items.zh: 这个字太难了。
items.py: zhè ge zì tài nán le
items.en: This character is too difficult.
items.why: 太 comes before the adjective and 了 closes the remark: 太难了. The 了 cannot be moved in front of 难.

items.src_py: zhè jiàn shì hěn zhòng yào
items.task: Say 'this matter is so important!' with 太.
items.zh: 这件事太重要了。
items.py: zhè jiàn shì tài zhòng yào le
items.en: This matter is so important!
items.why: A 太 remark replaces 很 and needs 了 at the end: 太重要了. 很 and 太 are not used together here.

items.s: 这个房间太了小。
items.s_py: zhè ge fáng jiān tài le xiǎo
items.zh: 这个房间太小了。
items.py: zhè ge fáng jiān tài xiǎo le
items.en: This room is too small.
items.why: 了 closes the 太 + adjective remark, so it goes after the adjective: 太小了. It cannot be placed between 太 and 小.

items.q: 我现在不喝咖啡___。
items.zh: 我现在不喝咖啡了。
items.py: wǒ xiàn zài bù hē kā fēi le
items.en: I don't drink coffee any more.
items.why: 'Not any more' is a change of situation, so 不 + verb takes 了 at the end. Without 了 it is a plain 'I don't drink coffee', with no sense of change.

items.q: 太晚了，我不去___。
items.zh: 太晚了，我不去了。
items.py: tài wǎn le wǒ bù qù le
items.en: It's too late, I'm not going after all.
items.why: A changed decision is 不 + verb + 了. 过 would refer to a past experience, 着 does not follow 去 here, and 吗 would turn it into a question.

items.q: 他已经不在这家公司工作___。
items.zh: 他已经不在这家公司工作了。
items.py: tā yǐ jīng bù zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò le
items.en: He doesn't work at this company any more.
items.why: 已经不 … 了 is 'no longer': the 了 at the end marks the change. 着 and 过 do not close this pattern, and 的 would need a noun.

items.q: 办公室里的咖啡喝完了，现在一点咖啡都没有___。
items.zh: 办公室里的咖啡喝完了，现在一点咖啡都没有了。
items.py: bàn gōng shì lǐ de kā fēi hē wán le xiàn zài yì diǎn kā fēi dōu méi yǒu le
items.en: The coffee in the office is finished, and now there's none left.
items.why: 没有 + noun + 了 says 'none left' as a new situation. 着 and 过 do not close this pattern, and 的 would require a noun after it.

items.q: 本来想去参加那个会，可是下雨了，所以我不想去___。
items.zh: 本来想去参加那个会，可是下雨了，所以我不想去了。
items.py: běn lái xiǎng qù cān jiā nà ge huì kě shì xià yǔ le suǒ yǐ wǒ bù xiǎng qù le
items.en: I originally wanted to go to that meeting, but it rained, so now I don't want to go.
items.why: A changed attitude is 不 + 想 + verb + 了. The earlier plan makes this a change of mind, which 着 and 过 cannot express.

items.q: 听说那个培训班要考试，我不报名___，还是自己在家学吧。
items.zh: 听说那个培训班要考试，我不报名了，还是自己在家学吧。
items.py: tīng shuō nà ge péi xùn bān yào kǎo shì wǒ bù bào míng le hái shì zì jǐ zài jiā xué ba
items.en: I heard that training course has an exam, so I won't sign up after all and will study at home.
items.why: 不报名了 expresses a changed decision after new information. 过 and 着 do not close the sentence, and 的 would require a noun. 还是 confirms the change of plan.

items.zh: 我不喝咖啡了。
items.py: wǒ bù hē kā fēi le
items.en: I don't drink coffee any more.
items.why: 不 + verb + 了 is the pattern for 'not any more': the 了 closes the sentence. Putting 了 after 喝 would turn it into a completed action.

items.zh: 下雨了我们不出去了。
items.py: xià yǔ le wǒ men bù chū qù le
items.en: It's raining, so we're not going out after all.
items.why: The 了 closes the sentence after 不出去 as a changed plan. The reason 下雨了 may come first or last, but 不出去了 stays as a unit.

items.zh: 因为天气不好我们不去旅行了。
items.py: yīn wèi tiān qì bù hǎo wǒ men bù qù lǚ xíng le
items.en: Because the weather is bad, we're not going on the trip after all.
items.why: 不 + verb + 了 shows the plan has changed. The 了 stays at the end, and 因为 can come before or after the subject.

items.src_py: wǒ xiǎng qù nà jiā gōng sī shàng bān
items.task: Say you changed your mind: you don't want to any more.
items.zh: 我不想去那家公司上班了。
items.py: wǒ bù xiǎng qù nà jiā gōng sī shàng bān le
items.en: I don't want to work at that company any more.
items.why: Changing 想 to 不想 plus a final 了 gives 'no longer want'. 了 must go at the end.

items.s: 我不吃了肉。
items.s_py: wǒ bù chī le ròu
items.zh: 我不吃肉了。
items.py: wǒ bù chī ròu le
items.en: I don't eat meat any more.
items.why: 'Not any more' puts 了 at the end of the whole clause: 不吃肉了. 了 cannot follow the verb directly here.

items.s: 太累了，我今天不加班了。
items.s_py: tài lèi le wǒ jīn tiān bù jiā bān le
items.zh: 太累了，我今天不加班了。
items.py: tài lèi le wǒ jīn tiān bù jiā bān le
items.en: I'm too tired, I'm not working overtime today after all.
items.why: This is correct: the second 了 closes 不加班 as a changed decision, and the first closes the 太 remark. Learners suspect two 了 are too many, but these are two different uses.
